newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close week on firm note.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close week on firm note.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed higher Friday, soaking up Wall Street's cheerful trading environment, dealers said.

"The markets in New York were spurred on today by the imminent budget deal in Washington, and they also reacted well to employment data," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "Here it seems we're slowly returning to an upward trend, helped by the strong profits of leading companies which should keep coming in next week."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.3 percent to 732.3, stretching gains in the week to 2.4 percent.
Floor volume slowed to 18.5 million pesos from 29.2 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover rose to 115.5 million pesos from 104.4 million Wednesday.
The market was closed Thursday for Labor Day.

"Bidding might start to pick up next week, especially with the release of quarterly profits of (oil holding company) Perez Companc which are likely to come in strong," another trader said. Perez Companc is the most liquid stock on the bolsa.
Heavyweights YPF and Telefonica announced strong earnings between Wednesday and Friday.
The broad market closed up 1.4 percent in the session, with winners outgunning losers 35 to eight and 18 stocks closing unchanged.

Top blue-chip gainers were carmaker Ciadea, foods giant Molinos and steelmaker Siderca, which rose 4.8 percent, 3.2 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively. Perez Companc gained 2.3 percent, Telecom 2.0 percent and Telefonica 1.2 percent.
Biggest MerVal losses were run up by construction stock Polledo, textile firm Alpargatas and Banco Frances, off 1.8 percent, 1.2 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.
